key_insight: LCGuard introduces a lightweight safeguard that sanitizes transformer key-value (KV) caches used for latent communication so agents can share rich intermediate signals without leaking contextual or agent-specific private information.
problem_solved: KV-based latent communication in LLM multi-agent systems can expose contextual inputs, intermediate reasoning states, and agent identity—existing defenses target natural-language channels and do not protect these opaque latent vectors.
method: Insert a learnable sanitizer (a projection/noise/transform module) that filters or transforms K/V cache vectors before sharing.
Train with a dual-objective: preserve task utility (downstream performance) while minimizing recoverable sensitive information via an adversarial discriminator or information-regularization loss.
Optionally include selective sharing (risk scoring) to only expose sanitized KV subsets based on context and sensitivity.
impact: Enables efficient, high-bandwidth latent communication among LLM agents while reducing private-information leakage—useful for collaborative systems in sensitive domains (health, finance, multi-agent planning). It balances performance and safety without reverting to verbose natural-language exchanges.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: LLM agent → KV cache → LCGuard sanitizer → shared KV → receiving agent, with icons for 'privacy' and 'utility'.
Before/after embedding projection (t-SNE) showing removal/obfuscation of sensitive clusters while preserving task-relevant structure.
Trade-off chart plotting task performance vs. information leakage/privacy metric across sanitizer strengths.
Icon set: multiple agents, shield/lock on KV stream, and a small adversary detector to indicate threat mitigation.
paper_title: LCGuard: Latent Communication Guard for Safe KV Sharing in Multi-Agent Systems
paper_authors: Sadia Asif, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Momin Abbas, Prasanna Sattigeri, Karthikeyan Natesan Ramamurthy
